name: Throw a football with a spiral
blurb: A tight spiral comes from grip and release, not arm strength. Fixing the fingertip position on the laces changes the ball’s behaviour immediately.
gear: Open space and a partner or a wall
steps: Set the grip: fingers on the laces, index finger near the back point, a gap between palm and ball.
Set the stance: non-throwing shoulder pointed at the target, ball held up near the ear.
Step towards the target with the front foot and rotate hips then shoulders — the arm follows the body.
Release over the top with the thumb finishing down past the opposite hip, and let the ball roll off the index finger last. That final fingertip is what puts on the spin.
Start ten metres apart and only add distance once the spirals are consistently tight.
Film in slow motion to check the ball leaves the index finger last.
tips: A wobbling ball is a release problem. Pushing the ball rather than snapping it off the fingers is the usual cause.
Throwing harder makes wobble worse. Perfect the release at short range first.
proof: Ten tight spirals in a row at 20 metres, on target.
